title: Recruit 3,000 police and reopen more than 40 stations
summary: The joint Liberal–Nationals plan pledges 3,000 more Victoria Police officers, filling existing vacancies and funding 1,500 additional officers, and reopening more than 40 police stations that have closed or had reduced hours. Recruitment would be accelerated, including from other jurisdictions, with a focus on retention.
sourceTitle: Reduce crime: 3,000 more police and Break Bail, Face Jail | Our Plan
excerpt: Our Plan will put 3,000 more police on the beat, by recruiting to fill existing vacancies, and funding an additional 1,500 officers.

title: Return PSOs to 119 stations and recruit 200 more
summary: The joint plan pledges 200 additional Protective Services Officers, their return to all 119 train stations where they were removed, and PSO strike teams patrolling high-risk shopping centres and precincts with powers to detect and remove knives and machetes. The plan also proposes strengthened Workplace Protection Orders and a police digital reporting platform for retail workers.
sourceTitle: Reduce crime: 3,000 more police and Break Bail, Face Jail | Our Plan
excerpt: Return PSOs to all 119 stations where they have been removed

title: Break Bail, Face Jail: one-strike bail rule
summary: The joint plan proposes a one-strike rule so repeat offending while on bail for 25 specified offences automatically results in refused bail for youth and adult offenders. It would also move bail applications for those offences to the County Court, make breach of bail a Schedule 2 offence, and remove the youth exemption for breaching bail conditions.
sourceTitle: Reduce crime: 3,000 more police and Break Bail, Face Jail | Our Plan
excerpt: If you break bail, you will face jail.

title: Adult Crime, Adult Time extended to 25 offences
summary: The joint plan would extend adult sentencing provisions to 25 serious offences, including arson, home invasion, carjacking, burglary and serious assault, with staged expansion based on relevant Queensland legislation. It also proposes a specialist Court of Criminal Appeal and an end to sentence discounts under Emergency Management Days.
sourceTitle: Reduce crime: 3,000 more police and Break Bail, Face Jail | Our Plan
excerpt: We will expand adult sentencing provisions to cover a broader range of 25 serious offences including arson, home invasion, carjacking, burglary and serious assault.

title: $100 million for early intervention and rehabilitation
summary: The joint plan commits $100 million to early intervention and crime prevention, including the residential Restart program for serious repeat offenders aged 12 to 17 and the community-based Youthstart initiative with Youth Justice Hubs, diversion, therapy, mentoring and family case management.
sourceTitle: Reduce crime: 3,000 more police and Break Bail, Face Jail | Our Plan
excerpt: Invest $100 million in early intervention and rehabilitation

title: Right to Ask, Right to Know domestic violence disclosure laws
summary: The joint plan proposes Clare's Law-style laws allowing people to ask police about a partner's known history of domestic violence and allowing police to disclose information where they judge someone to be at risk.
sourceTitle: Reduce crime: 3,000 more police and Break Bail, Face Jail | Our Plan
excerpt: That’s why we will introduce Right to Ask, Right to Know laws, creating a mechanism that allows people to find out if their partner has a known history of domestic abuse.

title: Guarantee of no new or increased taxes
summary: The joint plan commits a Liberal–Nationals government to no new or increased taxes on Victorian households and businesses, alongside specific tax abolition and relief measures.
sourceTitle: Lower costs: no new taxes, no stamp duty for first home buyers | Our Plan
excerpt: Our promise: no new or increased taxes.

title: Abolish the Emergency Services and Volunteers Fund levy
summary: The joint plan would abolish the levy on homes, businesses and farms that the parties call the 'Emergency Services Tax' — officially the Emergency Services and Volunteers Fund (ESVF), which replaced the Fire Services Property Levy on 1 July 2025. The Nationals say they would return to the Fire Services Property Levy.
sourceTitle: Lower costs: no new taxes, no stamp duty for first home buyers | Our Plan
excerpt: A Liberal and Nationals Government will scrap the Emergency Services Tax, which is a tax on every single family home, business and farm in the state.

title: Abolish the GP tax
summary: The joint plan pledges to abolish the tax on GP services that the parties call the 'GP Tax', which they say would reduce the cost of doctor visits and pressure on emergency departments.
sourceTitle: Lower costs: no new taxes, no stamp duty for first home buyers | Our Plan
excerpt: Our Plan will make it cheaper for Victorians to go to the GP by abolishing Labor’s regressive GP Tax.

title: Cap road tolls at $50 a week for two years
summary: The joint plan would cap road tolls at $50 per week for two years from 1 July 2027 for cars, light commercial vehicles and small business fleets of up to five vehicles. ABC News reports the cap as costed at $90 million a year.
sourceTitle: Lower costs: no new taxes, no stamp duty for first home buyers | Our Plan
excerpt: We will put a cap on road tolls so that Victorian families, tradies and small businesses will pay no more than $50 a week in tolls for two years from 1 July 2027.

title: Raise land tax-free threshold from $50,000 to $300,000
summary: The joint plan would lift the land tax threshold from $50,000 to $300,000 over five years. The parties say this would save 280,000 Victorians up to $975 a year.
sourceTitle: Lower costs: no new taxes, no stamp duty for first home buyers | Our Plan
excerpt: We will reverse Labor’s land tax hikes, lifting the land tax threshold from the current level of $50,000 back to the old level of $300,000 over a five year period, saving 280,000 Victorians up to $975 a year.

title: Remove payroll tax on government and non-government schools
summary: The joint plan would abolish the payroll tax on schools that the parties call the 'Schools Tax', so no Victorian government or non-government school would pay payroll tax.
sourceTitle: Lower costs: no new taxes, no stamp duty for first home buyers | Our Plan
excerpt: No Victorian government or non-government school will pay payroll tax under our commitment.

title: Payroll tax relief for 23,000 businesses
summary: The joint plan pledges payroll tax relief for 23,000 Victorian businesses. The Nationals' policy detail specifies lifting the payroll tax-free threshold from $1 million to $1.2 million over two years, then reducing the metropolitan payroll tax rate to 4.8 per cent from 2030-31.
sourceTitle: Lower costs: no new taxes, no stamp duty for first home buyers | Our Plan
excerpt: We will reduce costs for businesses, including by delivering payroll tax relief for 23,000 Victorian businesses.

title: Return budget to cash surplus by 2032
summary: The joint ten-year economic plan pledges a cash surplus by 2032. The parties say this would be achieved partly by a hiring freeze on back-office roles, which they estimate saves $22 billion, along with using windfall revenue to pay down debt and ending cost blowouts.
costing: $22 billion estimated saving from back-office hiring freeze (party figure)
sourceTitle: Our Ten Year Plan to secure Victoria’s economic future | Our Plan
excerpt: Our Plan returns Victoria to a cash surplus by 2032, stopping debt from rising further and beginning the long process of paying it down.

title: Repeal the Treaty process and First Peoples' Assembly
summary: The joint plan commits to repealing the Treaty process and First Peoples' Assembly within the first 100 days, which the parties say saves about $1 billion over a decade. ABC News reports PBO analysis putting the saving at roughly $948 million over the decade from 2025-26 to 2035-36.
costing: About $1 billion over a decade (party figure); about $948 million over a decade (PBO, as reported by ABC)
sourceTitle: Government that works: hospitals, schools, regions and integrity | Our Plan
excerpt: Stopping the $1 billion being spent on Labor’s divisive Treaty

title: $5 billion for roads and one million potholes
summary: The joint plan commits $5 billion over four years to rebuild, repair and resurface roads, including preventative maintenance and eliminating one million potholes. ABC News reports the figure as a 25 per cent increase on current road maintenance spending.
sourceTitle: Lower costs: no new taxes, no stamp duty for first home buyers | Our Plan
excerpt: Our Plan will invest $5 billion to rebuild, repair and resurface roads across Victoria, and do it properly.

title: Duplicate Donnybrook Road and extend Thompsons Road
summary: The joint plan pledges duplicating the full 8 km of Donnybrook Road from Epping Road, Woodstock to Dwyer Street, Kalkallo, and extending and duplicating Thompsons Road between Berwick-Cranbourne Road and Alexander Boulevard/Cardinia Road. ABC News reports costs of $524 million and $607 million respectively.
costing: $524 million (Donnybrook Road) and $607 million (Thompsons Road), as reported by ABC News
sourceTitle: Lower costs: no new taxes, no stamp duty for first home buyers | Our Plan
excerpt: Donnybrook Road duplication, duplicating the entire 8 km from Epping Rd, Woodstock to Dwyer St, Kalkallo, cutting travel times and congestion for one of Victoria’s fastest growing areas

title: Replace Swan Hill Bridge and progress Shepparton crossing
summary: The joint plan pledges replacing the 130-year-old Swan Hill Bridge to Murray Downs and planning, design and early works for a second Goulburn River crossing between Shepparton and Mooroopna. The Nationals state $25 million for the first stage of planning and development of the Shepparton crossing.
costing: $25 million for first-stage planning of the Second Goulburn River Crossing (Nationals figure)
sourceTitle: Lower costs: no new taxes, no stamp duty for first home buyers | Our Plan
excerpt: Swan Hill Bridge replacement, replacing the 130 year old bridge connecting Swan Hill to Murray Downs, improving traffic flow, freight and logistics and community safety

title: 25 hybrid electric trains for Melton and Wyndham Vale lines
summary: The joint plan pledges 25 new hybrid electric trains for the Melton and Wyndham Vale lines, with additional peak-hour City Loop services and more than double passenger capacity. ABC News reports a cost of $1.7 billion.
sourceTitle: Lower costs: no new taxes, no stamp duty for first home buyers | Our Plan
excerpt: We will deliver 25 new hybrid electric trains for the Melton and Wyndham Vale lines, finally delivering suburban rail services for these communities.

title: $288 million Country Roads and Bridges Program
summary: The joint plan pledges $288 million to restore the Country Roads and Bridges Program, giving each of Victoria's 48 rural and regional councils $1.5 million a year for four years in untied funding for local roads and bridges.
sourceTitle: Government that works: hospitals, schools, regions and integrity | Our Plan
excerpt: Each of Victoria’s 48 rural and regional councils will receive $1.5 million every year for four years to upgrade the local roads and bridges their communities rely on.

title: 25 additional three-car V/Line trains for regional Victoria
summary: The joint plan pledges 25 additional three-car V/Line trains for regional routes, with capacity shared across regions and a V'Locity set retained as a network reserve.
sourceTitle: Government that works: hospitals, schools, regions and integrity | Our Plan
excerpt: Under Our Plan an additional 25 three-car V/Line trains will be freed up for regional Victoria, boosting capacity, helping reduce crowding and keeping regional communities better connected.

title: $51.2 million Wimmera Mallee Rail Plan
summary: The joint plan pledges a Wimmera Mallee Rail Plan restoring passenger rail to western and north-western Victoria, with three services a week between Mildura and Melbourne connecting at Maryborough and three a week between Dimboola and Melbourne. The Nationals state a cost of $51.2 million.
sourceTitle: Government that works: hospitals, schools, regions and integrity | Our Plan
excerpt: We will also deliver a Wimmera Mallee Rail Plan to restore regular passenger rail services across western and north-western Victoria, improving connectivity and growing access to jobs, education, healthcare and services.

title: Stamp duty exemption for first home buyers up to $1 million
summary: The joint plan would exempt first home buyers from stamp duty on homes valued up to $1 million. The Nationals say the exemption would cover established and off-the-plan properties, and cite a PBO estimate of more than 17,000 exemptions in the first full year.
sourceTitle: Lower costs: no new taxes, no stamp duty for first home buyers | Our Plan
excerpt: We will exempt first home buyers from stamp duty on properties valued up to $1 million.

title: Fast-track housing supply and planning approvals
summary: The joint plan pledges end dates for all Precinct Structure Plans, industry-led PSPs, and spending Growth Areas Infrastructure Contribution revenue in the communities where it is raised. It also proposes set timeframes and fees for cultural heritage approvals and annual audits of heritage and Melbourne Water approvals.
sourceTitle: Lower costs: no new taxes, no stamp duty for first home buyers | Our Plan
excerpt: Our Plan will set clear end dates from commencement for all PSPs and introduce industry-led PSPs to speed up land release and increase housing supply.

title: Restore local planning control and scrap activity centres
summary: The joint plan pledges returning planning decisions to local communities and scrapping the government's high-rise activity centres policy. It also proposes ending heritage-related delays and setting approval timeframes.
sourceTitle: Lower costs: no new taxes, no stamp duty for first home buyers | Our Plan
excerpt: A Liberal and Nationals Government will restore local planning control and return decision-making to local communities.

title: Expand the Capital City Zone around the CBD
summary: The joint plan would expand the Capital City Zone into targeted inner-city areas around the CBD that are already serviced by public transport, aiming to increase apartment supply.
sourceTitle: Lower costs: no new taxes, no stamp duty for first home buyers | Our Plan
excerpt: Our Plan will expand the Capital City Zone into targeted parts of the inner city surrounding the CBD, building on certainty, streamlined approvals and mixed-use flexibility, in areas already serviced by public transport.

title: Reintroduce 10 Technical Colleges
summary: The joint plan pledges 10 dedicated technical secondary colleges across metropolitan and regional Victoria for up to 5,000 students a year, with free industry-focused Years 10–12 education and VCE certificates. ABC News reports a cost of $222 million.
sourceTitle: Lower costs: no new taxes, no stamp duty for first home buyers | Our Plan
excerpt: We will reintroduce proper Technical Colleges in Victoria, delivering 10 dedicated secondary colleges across metropolitan and regional Victoria for up to 5,000 students each year.

title: Accelerating Apprenticeships Fund
summary: The joint plan would cover half the off-the-job training costs for apprentices in trades on the Australian Apprenticeships Priority List. ABC News reports a cost of $115 million.
sourceTitle: Lower costs: no new taxes, no stamp duty for first home buyers | Our Plan
excerpt: Our Plan will cover half the off-the-job training costs for apprentices in trades listed on the Australian Apprenticeships Priority List, reducing the costs currently paid by employers

title: Literacy and Numeracy Guarantee with NAPLAN targets
summary: The joint plan pledges a Literacy and Numeracy Guarantee with an interim target of a 15 per cent increase in students proficient under NAPLAN and a long-term goal of 90 per cent proficiency, plus teacher professional learning, a curriculum review and three new select-entry high schools before 2030.
sourceTitle: Government that works: hospitals, schools, regions and integrity | Our Plan
excerpt: The Guarantee includes an interim target of a 15% increase in the number of kids deemed proficient in literacy and numeracy under NAPLAN.

title: Improve ambulance response times and build new stations
summary: The joint plan would place experienced paramedics in the Triple Zero call-taking process and build new ambulance stations at Armstrong Creek, Mansfield and Donnybrook, with the aim of improving dispatch decisions and response times.
sourceTitle: Government that works: hospitals, schools, regions and integrity | Our Plan
excerpt: We will put experienced paramedics into the Triple Zero call-taking process to improve dispatch decisions and ensure a focus on priority responses.

title: Deploy 70 PSOs across seven major hospitals
summary: The joint plan pledges 70 Protective Services Officers across seven major hospitals to provide around-the-clock security and reduce assaults on health workers.
sourceTitle: Government that works: hospitals, schools, regions and integrity | Our Plan
excerpt: We will improve safety at hospitals to reduce assaults on our health workers by deploying 70 Protective Services Officers across 7 major hospitals, providing around-the-clock security.

title: SurgerySooner: 25,000 extra elective surgeries a year
summary: The joint plan pledges 25,000 additional elective surgeries each year by partnering with private hospitals and day surgeries, at no extra cost to patients. ABC News reports a cost of $1.27 billion, funded by scrapping the government's Breakthrough Victoria investment fund.
sourceTitle: Government that works: hospitals, schools, regions and integrity | Our Plan
excerpt: Based on a successful Queensland program, our SurgerySooner plan will deliver 25,000 extra elective surgeries each year, working with private surgical hospitals and day surgeries across Victoria.

title: Establish Australia's first proton beam therapy service
summary: The joint pledges support for establishing Australia's first proton beam therapy service at the Peter MacCallum Cancer Centre, so patients would not need to travel overseas for the treatment.
sourceTitle: Government that works: hospitals, schools, regions and integrity | Our Plan
excerpt: support the establishment of Australia’s first proton beam therapy service at Victoria’s world leading Peter MacCallum Cancer Centre

title: $63.5 million for mental health early intervention
summary: The joint plan commits $63.5 million to local communities through a Mental Health Early Access Plan and almost $70 million to statewide support services, including crisis support, suicide prevention, youth mental health, counselling and parent support.
costing: $63.5 million for local early intervention and almost $70 million for statewide services (party figures)
sourceTitle: Government that works: hospitals, schools, regions and integrity | Our Plan
excerpt: This includes $63.5 million invested into local communities to expand early intervention, build community capability and reduce pressure on acute services as part of our Mental Health Early Access Plan.

title: Youth mental health facility, centre and workforce fund
summary: The joint plan pledges $5 million for a masterplan for a standalone youth mental health facility at Parkville with up to 50 beds for people aged 12 to 25, a Youth Mental Health Centre of Excellence with Orygen, and a $50 million Targeted Mental Health Workforce Fund within the first 100 days.
costing: $5 million for the Parkville masterplan and $50 million workforce fund (party figures)
sourceTitle: Government that works: hospitals, schools, regions and integrity | Our Plan
excerpt: Invest $5 million to deliver the masterplan for a standalone youth mental health facility at Parkville, with up to 50 specialist youth inpatient beds for Victorians aged 12 to 25

title: Upgrade regional hospitals and rural health workforce
summary: The joint plan pledges upgrades to hospitals in Mildura, West Gippsland, Wonthaggi, Hamilton, Colac, Bairnsdale, Rosebud, Albury Wodonga and the Goulburn Valley. It also offers eligible rural doctors, nurses, midwives and allied health workers up to $10,000 a year; the Nationals put a $40 million four-year cost on that scheme.
costing: Regional hospital figures reported by ABC News: $850m West Gippsland, $350m Wonthaggi, $180m Mildura, $100m Albury Wodonga, $45m Hamilton; $40 million over four years for rural health incentives (Nationals figure)
sourceTitle: Government that works: hospitals, schools, regions and integrity | Our Plan
excerpt: eligible doctors, nurses, midwives and allied health professionals will be offered incentives of up to $10,000 a year to fill critical jobs in rural and regional Victoria

title: Establish an Energy Security Requirement
summary: The joint plan pledges a technology-agnostic Energy Security Requirement to identify commercial proposals for firming capacity and energy security without preferencing or excluding particular energy sources.
sourceTitle: Lower costs: no new taxes, no stamp duty for first home buyers | Our Plan
excerpt: We will establish an Energy Security Requirement for Victoria to address the forecast energy shortfall and ensure reliable and affordable power.

title: End gas appliance ban and reopen gas exploration
summary: The joint plan pledges scrapping the ban on gas appliances in new homes and reopening gas exploration, which the parties say would restore consumer choice and increase local gas supply.
sourceTitle: Lower costs: no new taxes, no stamp duty for first home buyers | Our Plan
excerpt: Our Plan will throw open the door for gas exploration, ensuring reliable gas supply for Victoria, supporting manufacturing and helping our gas industry create more local jobs.

title: Establish Urban Solar Parks
summary: The joint plan pledges new Urban Solar Parks to encourage solar and battery installations on commercial and industrial rooftops in urban areas, generating renewable power closer to demand.
sourceTitle: Lower costs: no new taxes, no stamp duty for first home buyers | Our Plan
excerpt: The Liberals and Nationals will establish new Urban Solar Parks to encourage solar and battery installations on commercial and industrial rooftops in urban areas, generating renewable power closer to where it is needed.

title: $50 million Coastal Environment Resilience Fund and waste changes
summary: The joint plan's booklet pledges a $50 million Coastal Environment Resilience Fund for erosion repairs and longer-term protection. It also pledges scrapping the mandatory fourth bin, requiring councils to provide weekly general rubbish collection, doubling planned fire mitigation burns and establishing a $15 million horticulture centre of excellence.
costing: $50 million Coastal Environment Resilience Fund and $15 million Horticulture Centre of Excellence (party figures)
sourceTitle: Our Plan to Deliver for Victorians — 2026 online booklet
excerpt: And we will create a dedicated $50 million Coastal Environment Resilience Fund to manage immediate coastal erosion repairs, as well as investing in longer-term protection measures.

title: Enhanced Royal Commission into CFMEU misconduct
summary: The joint plan pledges an enhanced Royal Commission into conduct linked to the CFMEU, investigating allegations of corruption and unlawful behaviour in the construction sector, alongside a Victoria Police taskforce working with the AFP and ATO to seize assets.
sourceTitle: Government that works: hospitals, schools, regions and integrity | Our Plan
excerpt: An enhanced Royal Commission into CFMEU misconduct, investigating allegations of corruption and unlawful behaviour within the construction sector

title: Legislated Charter of Budget Honesty
summary: The joint plan pledges a legislated Charter of Budget Honesty requiring governments to deliver clear, accurate financial reports, to be introduced in the first 100 days.
sourceTitle: Government that works: hospitals, schools, regions and integrity | Our Plan
excerpt: A legislated Charter of Budget Honesty requiring governments to deliver clear, accurate financial reports to restore trust in government

title: Real-time Public Spending Tracker
summary: The joint plan pledges a Public Spending Tracker allowing Victorians to see how taxpayer money is spent, monitor major projects and view departmental budgets, with development to start in the first 100 days.
sourceTitle: Government that works: hospitals, schools, regions and integrity | Our Plan
excerpt: A Public Spending Tracker to allow Victorians to see how taxpayer money is being spent, and to monitor major projects and departmental budgets

title: Construction Enforcement Victoria and site background checks
summary: The joint plan pledges a new watchdog, Construction Enforcement Victoria, to enforce a code of practice and prosecute crimes on taxpayer-funded sites. It also proposes mandatory criminal history checks and bans on people with links to organised crime working on major projects, plus US-style racketeering laws.
sourceTitle: Government that works: hospitals, schools, regions and integrity | Our Plan
excerpt: We will establish Construction Enforcement Victoria, an independent watchdog with real teeth to get tough on the rorts and prosecute crimes, with a Victorian Code of Practice for the Building and Construction Industry for all taxpayer-funded construction sites.

title: 25 per cent Fair Share Guarantee for regional infrastructure
summary: The joint plan pledges that at least 25 per cent of infrastructure spending would go to regional Victoria, where about 25 per cent of the population lives. The parties say the current regional share is 12 per cent, and commit to begin implementation within the first 100 days.
sourceTitle: Government that works: hospitals, schools, regions and integrity | Our Plan
excerpt: Our Fair Share Guarantee means the 25% of Victorians who live in regional Victoria will get a minimum of 25% of infrastructure spending allocated to them.

title: $40 million Major Events Attraction Fund
summary: A November 2026 announcement commits a Liberal–Nationals government to a $40 million Major Events Attraction Fund to attract major sporting and entertainment events to Melbourne, including UFC, WWE and Zuffa Boxing events, working with TKO in its first term.
sourceTitle: Wilson commits to bring UFC back to Melbourne in Major Events knockout | Liberal Victoria
excerpt: A Jess Wilson-led Liberal and Nationals Government will establish a $40 million Major Events Attraction Fund to bring major sporting and entertainment events to Melbourne, including UFC.
